decision.reason: Persistent glaciers, polar ice sheets/fields and sea ice share reusable load-bearing frozen-surface and ice-mass behavior that is neither ordinary Open Country nor Highland: traction, fracture/crevasse or lead formation, melt channels, surface relief, unstable edges and slow movement/deformation of the substrate itself. Generic cold, snow, blizzard severity and physiological exposure remain overlay or local-condition authority rather than archetype identity.

archetypes.name: Persistent Ice / Cryosphere
archetypes.baseline_scope: Persistent load-bearing ice masses or ice surfaces where traversal, fracture, crevasses/leads, melt features, unstable edges and slow substrate movement shape navigation and exposure independently of generic cold severity.
reusable_behavior: fracture crevasse lead and weak-zone hazards
meltwater channels pools and refrozen surfaces
ice ridges hummocks pressure features and surface relief
unstable or calving edges where the local form permits
slow substrate drift flow or deformation
excluded_or_deferred: exact temperature band or Extreme Cold
specific travel equipment or vehicle mechanics
evidence_basis: ENV-03 explicit ice/glacier traversal gap watch item
owner-approved ENV-09 Glacier/Icefield, Polar Ice and Sea Ice expansion scope

non_promotions.reason: Tree-dominated route-finding, canopy/sightline and shelter behavior is already owned by Forest; cold/snow are separate conditions.
Treeless exposed terrain, long sightlines and sparse fixed shelter are already represented by Open Country; permafrost/cold remain preset or later physical-condition detail.
Steep terrain, elevation change, passes and fall/rock hazards are already owned by Highland; cold, snow and low oxygen remain later conditions/overlays.
Sea ice is persistent traversable ice over marine water and therefore combines ice-surface behavior with open-water context instead of requiring a separate marine-ice archetype.
